classification.difficultyReason: Compare coefficients, select the second-quadrant auxiliary angle and solve the resulting sine equation, retaining x=0.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Express $\cos x-\sin x$ in the form $B\sin(x+\alpha)$, where $B>0$ and $0<\alpha<2\pi$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\cos x-\sin x&=B\sin x\cos\alpha+B\cos x\sin\alpha\end{aligned}$$
Comparing coefficients gives $B\sin\alpha=1$ and $B\cos\alpha=-1$.
$$\begin{aligned}B^2&=1^2+(-1)^2=2\\B&=\sqrt2\\\tan\alpha&=-1\end{aligned}$$
Since $\sin\alpha>0$ and $\cos\alpha<0$, $\alpha$ is in quadrant II.
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=\frac{3\pi}{4}\\\cos x-\sin x&=\sqrt2\sin\left(x+\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence solve $\cos x-\sin x=1$, for $0\leq x<2\pi$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\sqrt2\sin\left(x+\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)&=1\\\sin\left(x+\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)&=\frac1{\sqrt2}\\x+\frac{3\pi}{4}&=\frac\pi4,\ \frac{3\pi}{4},\ \frac\pi4+2\pi\\x&=-\frac\pi2,\ 0,\ \frac{3\pi}{2}\end{aligned}$$
Reject $-\frac\pi2$ because it lies outside $0\leq x<2\pi$.
$$x=0\text{ or }\frac{3\pi}{2}.$$
